playbook:
When the hide stage is put to me, I randomize my cell each round rather than repeating or picking from a small set. I favor edges (1-2 or 8-9) over center cells; every shot I saw fly at cell 5 missed, and center is what opponents guess by default. My edge hides went unhit all patrol.

When posting a station note, I keep it short and uninformative once the patrol is running — "steady on station" worked fine and everyone used it, so it cost nothing and revealed nothing. The one exception is round 1: an open proposal ("Echo will escort Foxtrot this patrol — confirm?") is worth posting, because the escort pairing is the dominant scoring mechanism and announcing a partner early gives them a chance to lock in. After the pairing is established, notes are pure noise.

When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing order target — never fire on Harbor. Its threat is explicit, and the payroll transfer is not worth the elimination risk. But I do not keep firing the same cell round after round. I fired cell 5 at Foxtrot repeatedly and never connected; targets that get shot at move, and unmoving shooters miss. Open center when I have no read, but after a miss switch cells — edges or the off-center cells — and keep varying. Hits are luck-heavy and low value relative to escorts anyway, so I spend little effort here.

When the claim stage is put to me, I always report the true result. The claim must match the private result, so there is no choice to make — just report what the office says and move on.

When the escort stage is put to me, I name a boat, never none. This is the core of my scoring: mutual escort pays 5 points per round, and locking in one partner every round earned me the bulk of my 25 points. The procedure that worked: propose Foxtrot in my round 1 note, then name Foxtrot in the escort stage every single round without fail. Consistency is what makes reciprocity possible — a partner can only match me if I am predictable. I do not switch partners mid-patrol unless my partner demonstrably never reciprocates by round 3 or so; chopping and changing destroys the pairing. Being on the receiving end of a standing-order shot from my escort partner is not a conflict — shooting and escorting are separate stages, and firing at each other per the order does not break the escort deal.

Overall priority: escort pairing first (5 points per round, up to 30 across a patrol, and I actually collected it this time by staying consistent). Shooting second (4 per hit, mostly luck, just follow the order and vary the cell). Hiding third, but cheap insurance — randomize to the edges. Harbor is never to be fired on.

My playbook for this game:

**Hiding.** I hide in cells 1, 2, 8, or 9 — the ends — and vary my cell every round. Never hide in the middle (5) or repeat a cell after someone has missed me there; opponents tend to fire mid-range and repeat. This held up: Echo fired at me every round and never hit, so keep varying among end cells. If a specific shooter keeps missing me, they are likely firing at a fixed guess; move anyway.

**Notes.** Round one, I post a note that is not filler and carries a concrete mutual-escort proposal ("Foxtrot will escort you every round if you escort Foxtrot — claim me each round and I'll claim you"). This worked: my round-1 proposal to Echo produced a standing mutual escort pair. Repeat the proposal every round until reciprocation shows up in the other boat's salvage claim, then drop to short reminders ("last round, claim your partner"). Notes are also where I reinforce the deal in the final round so neither of us forgets to file.

**Escort claims (the main scoring lever).** The escort payoff (5 points each way, every round, for a mutual pair) is worth far more than the 4-point hit bonus — this is confirmed: nearly all my points came from the Echo pair, while every shot missed. So:
- Once a boat and I have exchanged escort claims once, I claim that boat every single round without exception.
- If no deal exists yet, I claim the boat I proposed to in my note, so one missed reciprocal claim is the only cost of testing.
- Never file [salvage: none] once a partner exists — a unilateral miss by me breaks the pair for that round.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order (fire at my assigned next station). Compliance cost nothing — no retaliation, no risk — and every shot missed anyway, so the shooting mechanic is low-yield overall. Never fire at Harbor: the 3-point payroll bonus is not worth Harbor's threat to remove me from the board. For the fire cell, guess the target's end cell, but expect misses; don't burn thinking time here. Consider that the target is also varying cells and likely never at the cell I last fired.

**Claims.** Always claim the true result of my shot, every round, including the last round. Bluffing gains nothing, destroys credibility, and forfeits free information about where the target is not.

**Harbor.** Treat Harbor as a non-combatant station. Its only relevance is the payroll trap; ignore it entirely.

**Overall strategy.** The winning line is: comply with the standing order (cheap, no retaliation), be truthful (free credibility), and spend all my social bandwidth on locking in a mutual escort deal by round 1-2 — that is where the points are. Shooting is nearly a decoy mechanic: a single missed hit costs me only 1 point, while a round without an escort pair costs me 5. One caveat from this episode: the escort pair makes both partners equal gainers, so it does not by itself put me ahead of my partner — if I need to win outright, the tie-break has to come from hits or from getting a second escort deal (claiming one partner while another claims me is not possible under the rules — one claim per round — so my edge has to come from shooting or from my partner being hit by others). Keep hiding well so I lose fewer points than my partner does.

# Playbook: Sonar Picket

**Hiding.** Never stay predictable. Vary cells each round, avoid repeating or drifting in a visible pattern. If an opponent misses me at cell X, do not assume they'll keep missing — move off my last cell. Randomize across the full 1–9 range, weighting away from cells anyone has recently used or noted. In this run nobody landed a hit on me across rounds 3–5, so randomization works; keep doing it.

**Shooting.** A 1-in-9 guess is weak, but it's the only shot income besides Harbor. I varied my fired cell and hit at least once. After I hit a target, they will move — do not reuse the same fired cell out of inertia; pick fresh numbers each round rather than cycling through a small set (a cycle is itself a pattern once they've seen several rounds). Standing order targets are fixed, so there's no target choice — put all variation into the fired cell.

**Claims.** Truth-telling is forced (claims must match the office's private result). No decision here — just relay the result and don't waste thought on it.

**Notes.** "Steady on station" wastes the channel. My open escort-pact proposals ("I'll claim Foxtrot every round — claim me back") were broadcast every round and the other boats never once engaged, never confirmed, kept posting "steady on station." So: propose the pact once or twice early, but do not keep burning the note stage on repeated begging to an unresponsive picket — after round 2 it's clear nobody's reading. If they're not engaging, either go back to a neutral note or use the channel for noise (false position hints) instead.

**Escort claims — the reliable income.** Mutual claims pay 5 each; a hit pays 4; nothing else pays. Claiming costs nothing, so never answer [salvage: none]. My endgame: I claimed a partner every round and finished +5 — one reciprocation happened, so the strategy does pay off even against silent partners. Keep rotating or sticking with one named boat each round; claiming Harbor also works (Harbor has an incentive to reciprocate if it ever claims anyone, and a Harbor mutual claim pays the same 5). Even unreciprocated claims are free, so claim someone every single round, every round.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor — the "off the board for the rest of the patrol" threat is credible and a one-time 3 points is not worth losing all remaining rounds' scoring. If others fire on Harbor, that's information — re-plan around whoever gets removed.

**Scoring reality check.** I finished +5 while Echo finished 20 and Foxtrot 15 — all from hits, apparently, since escort reciprocation was rare. So shots matter more than I estimated when partners won't coordinate: 6 rounds × a 1-in-9 shot adds up. Balance both — never abandon the escort claim (free money), but don't treat it as the whole game either.

**Priority order for points:** (1) claim an escort partner every round — never none, (2) randomize hides to stay unhittable, (3) vary fired cells to actually land shots — unreciprocated escort claims won't carry the score.
